known_facts_book1: A small boy from a far corner of the Gillikin Country, near Oogaboo, who left home because his friends were so quiet and happy and comfortable that he found them dismally stupid.
Has been a wanderer for nearly a full year, and says the more he wanders the less he finds that he knows.
Is the one who tells the Tin Woodman that deserting Nimmie Amee was unkind, and so is the cause of the whole journey.
Bursts his bonds at Loonville when a thorn pricks his leg, and routs the whole tribe by chasing them with that same thorn, popping them one after another.
Is transformed by Mrs. Yoop into a **Green Monkey** with silk-like green fur, and is made contented with the form by an extra bit of her magic.
Steals the Magic Lace Apron from the bedpost while the Giantess snores, pushes a giant chair under the birdcage to reach Polychrome, and locks Mrs. Yoop in her own bedroom.
Escapes the Jaguar by shouting 'Open!' while wearing the Apron, and falls straight through the earth into the cavern of the Dragons.
Escapes the Dragons the same way, opening a hole in the cavern roof above his head.
Is scrubbed in a tub of cold water by Jinjur after climbing up her chimney, and dried with a coarse towel.
**Cannot be restored by Ozma or by Glinda**: the Green Monkey must exist in the Land of Oz for all future time and can only be transferred to someone else.
Refuses to let the form be put on Toto or on anyone else, saying it would be wicked to ask another to take his place.
Is restored only when Ozma, at Polychrome's suggestion, gives the Green Monkey's form to Mrs. Yoop herself.
Is allowed by Ozma at the end to wander wherever he desires, with her promise to watch over him.

known_relations_book1.Tin Woodman: Whose conscience he pricks, starting the quest.
known_relations_book1.Polychrome: The fairy whose idea finally frees him.
known_relations_book1.Mrs. Yoop: The Giantess who makes him a Green Monkey and ends up wearing the form herself.
known_relations_book1.Jinjur: Who scrubs him and comforts him.

known_facts_book1: The Tin Woodman's best friend, a suit of clothes stuffed with straw whose head is a gunnysack of bran with a painted face.
Was made by a Munchkin farmer in the very forest the party travels through, and his current painted expression was done by Jinjur about a month before the transformations.
Recites poems learned from Professor Wogglebug, including one in praise of straw stuffing.
Is transformed by Mrs. Yoop into a **little Brown Bear**, still stuffed with straw and just as wobbly, after telling the Giantess she is acting like a bear.
Is the easiest of the four to restore, since even yookoohoo magic could only make a straw-stuffed bear out of a straw-stuffed man.
Sacrifices his own straw stuffing to the Hip-po-gy-raf so the party can be lifted over the ditch, and is restuffed with hay by Woot and Polychrome — badly, with a hump on his back.
Gets proper straw again at the Swynes' straw-stack, and is so pleased he tries to dance a jig.
Argues that thoughts should be restrained like the Tin Woodman's oil, applied only when necessary and for a good purpose.
Is the one who suggests the exchange of forms as a way to free Woot, though the version that works is Polychrome's.
Refuses Ku-Klip's offer to remake him in tin, saying he likes himself better as he is.

known_relations_book1.Tin Woodman: His best friend, whom he accompanies without hesitation.
known_relations_book1.Jinjur: The friend who repaints his face and once painted him a straw-stack.
known_relations_book1.the Hip-po-gy-raf: The beast he feeds his own stuffing to.

known_facts_book1: A Sky Fairy, daughter of the Rainbow, who danced off her bow after a rain and fell asleep on a mound in Mrs. Yoop's valley.
Was transformed by the sleeping Giantess into a **Canary-Bird** in a gold cage studded with diamonds, and refused to speak a single word for weeks.
Says she could easily have protected herself had she been awake; the Giantess took unfair advantage of her.
Is the one who discovers that only the **Magic Lace Apron** can open the doors and windows of Yoop Castle, having watched Mrs. Yoop forget to put it on one morning.
Knows the Giantess still has six magic hairpins, an invisible magic ring on her thumb and magic bracelets on both ankles, so she is not really trapped.
Conjures scrambled eggs on toast for the hungry Jaguar rather than let it eat any living thing.
Removes ten of Tommy Kwikstep's twenty legs — and the corns from the ten toes she leaves him.
Oils Captain Fyter's jaws with the Tin Woodman's oil-can and so frees him from years of rust.
Mends the Tin Soldier's bent leg and the dent in the Tin Woodman's side with rhymed fairy charms, remarking that her magic works splendidly on tin.
Shrinks the entire party small enough to pass through the Blue Rabbit's burrow under the Wall of Solid Air, and enlarges them again.
Is restored by Ozma only after a chain of experiments: Canary to Dove to Speckled Hen to rabbit to Fawn, then powders sprinkled on the Fawn.
Proposes the solution that frees Woot: give the Green Monkey's form to the woman who created it.
Leaves on her Rainbow at the very end, after the storm, having kissed Woot lightly on the forehead.

known_relations_book1.Mrs. Yoop: The Giantess who caught her asleep and caged her.
known_relations_book1.Woot: The boy she frees twice — once from the castle, once from the monkey form.
known_relations_book1.Captain Fyter: The Tin Soldier she unrusts and later mends.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler who breaks her enchantment after several failures.
